# **I. Introduction**

## **1\. Product Background**

The rapid growth of digital learning has resulted in a significant increase in the amount of educational material that students need to study. At FPT University, students may work with various types of learning materials, including lecture slides, course syllabi, laboratory guides, assignment descriptions, technical documents, and other course-related resources.

Students often use general-purpose AI tools to summarize documents, ask questions, and generate practice quizzes. However, general AI systems may generate questions that are:

* Outside the provided course materials  
* Inconsistent with the course learning outcomes  
* Based on information that does not exist in the source documents  
* Difficult to verify  
* Missing references to the original learning materials

This creates a problem of **uncontrolled AI-generated learning content**.

The **FPT RAG Lab – Outcome-Aligned Quiz Generation Platform** is proposed to address this problem by combining **Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)** with structured course information and predefined learning outcomes.

The system allows students to upload course materials into an isolated workspace and generate multiple-choice quizzes based strictly on the uploaded documents and defined learning outcomes.

Each generated question should contain a citation to the source material whenever sufficient supporting information is available.

---

# **2\. Existing Systems**

## **2.1 General AI Chatbots**

Modern AI chatbots provide capabilities such as:

* Question answering  
* Text summarization  
* Content generation  
* Quiz generation  
* Document analysis

Students can provide course materials and ask an AI system to generate questions.

### **Limitations**

General-purpose AI systems may have the following limitations:

* Generated content may not strictly follow the uploaded documents  
* Questions may include external knowledge  
* Learning outcomes may not be explicitly considered  
* Source citations may be unavailable or incomplete  
* Users may have difficulty verifying the origin of generated questions  
* Different users may not have strict data isolation

---

## **2.2 Traditional Quiz Generation Methods**

Traditional quiz creation generally requires instructors or teaching assistants to manually create questions from course materials.

Typical processes include:

* Reading lecture materials  
* Identifying important topics  
* Creating questions  
* Creating answer choices  
* Reviewing answers  
* Mapping questions to learning outcomes

### **Limitations**

Manual quiz creation can result in:

* High time consumption  
* Repetitive work  
* Difficulty generating large question sets  
* Inconsistent question coverage  
* Difficulty maintaining question-source references  
* Additional effort when course materials change

---

# **3\. Business Opportunity**

The increasing use of AI in education creates an opportunity to build an AI-assisted learning platform specifically designed around **course materials and learning outcomes**.

For students, the platform can provide:

* Faster quiz generation  
* Course-specific practice  
* Questions based on uploaded materials  
* Source citations  
* Learning-outcome-oriented practice  
* Saved quizzes for later study

For educational organizations, the platform can provide:

* Centralized course materials  
* Controlled AI-generated learning content  
* Better traceability of generated questions  
* Course-level data isolation  
* Reusable quiz banks  
* Potential future integration with university learning systems

The platform can also provide an environment where students can learn how RAG systems work through practical interaction with document retrieval, embeddings, vector databases, and LLM-based generation.

---

# **4\. Software Product Vision**

The goal of the **FPT RAG Lab** is to provide a reliable AI-assisted learning platform that generates practice quizzes from course materials while maintaining strong grounding, traceability, and alignment with learning outcomes.

The system aims to:

* Allow students to upload course-related documents  
* Organize documents by course/workspace  
* Retrieve relevant information from uploaded documents  
* Generate questions based on retrieved content  
* Align questions with predefined learning outcomes  
* Provide citations for generated questions  
* Refuse to generate questions when sufficient source information cannot be found  
* Prevent unauthorized access to other users' documents  
* Save generated quizzes for future study  
* Reduce unnecessary repeated LLM processing

### **Vision Statement**

> **“Provide an outcome-aligned and source-grounded AI learning environment that helps FPT students generate reliable practice quizzes directly from their course materials.”**

# **6\. Limitations and Exclusions**

## **Limitations**

The system has the following limitations:

* Quiz quality depends on the quality of uploaded documents  
* Scanned documents may require OCR processing  
* LLM-generated content may require validation  
* Large documents require additional processing time  
* AI API availability affects quiz generation  
* Vector search quality depends on chunking and embedding configuration  
* The system requires an internet connection for cloud-based AI services  
* Uploaded documents must comply with supported file formats and size limits

---

## **Exclusions (Out-of-Scope)**

The following functionalities are not included in the current system scope:

* Automatic grading of written essays  
* Full Learning Management System (LMS)  
* Online video lectures  
* Live online classes  
* Student-to-student social networking  
* Automatic course enrollment through university systems  
* Automatic modification of official FPT course materials  
* AI-generated lecture materials as a replacement for instructors  
* Facial recognition  
* Voice-based examination  
* Online proctoring  
* Automatic academic certification  
* University-wide student information system replacement

# **II. Overall Description**

## **1\. Product Overview**

The **FPT RAG Lab – Outcome-Aligned Quiz Generation Platform** is a web-based AI learning platform designed to help FPT students generate practice quizzes directly from their course materials.

The system combines a conventional backend with a dedicated AI/RAG processing service. Students can select a course, upload PDF/DOCX learning materials, select learning outcomes, and generate quizzes based on the content retrieved from their own documents.

The system consists of the following major components:

* **Student Web Application**  
* **ASP.NET Core Backend**  
* **Python AI/RAG Service**  
* **PostgreSQL Database**  
* **pgvector Vector Database**  
* **LLM API**  
* **Administrator Management Module**

The overall system architecture is illustrated below:

&nbsp;

# **2\. Business Process**

The main business processes of the **FPT RAG Lab** are divided into three major workflows:

### **2.1 Document Upload and Processing Process**

Student uploads course materials → Backend validates the request → Python AI Service processes the document → Document is chunked and embedded → Embeddings are stored in pgvector → Document becomes available for quiz generation.

### **2.2 Outcome-Aligned Quiz Generation Process**

Student selects Course and Learning Outcomes → Backend validates authentication, workspace permission, and token quota → Python AI Service creates a retrieval query → pgvector retrieves relevant document chunks → RAG context is constructed → LLM generates questions → System validates structure, course grounding, learning-outcome alignment, and citations → Quiz is saved and returned to Student.

### **2.3 Quiz Execution and Scoring Process**

Student opens a generated quiz → Reads questions → Selects answers → Submits quiz → Backend validates submission → System retrieves correct answers → Calculates score → Saves quiz attempt → Returns score, explanations, and citations → Student can review quiz history.

### 2.1 Document Upload and Processing Process — Process Step Description

| \# | Process Step | Description |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| 1 | Select Course / Workspace | Student selects the course or workspace where the document will be stored. |
| 2 | Select Document | Student selects a PDF or DOCX course material. |
| 3 | Upload Document | Student submits the selected document to the system. |
| 4 | Authenticate Student | Backend verifies the student's authentication information. |
| 5 | Check Workspace Permission | System verifies that the student has permission to access the selected workspace. |
| 6 | Validate File Type | System verifies that the uploaded file is a supported PDF or DOCX document. |
| 7 | Validate File Size | System checks whether the document is within the configured file-size limit. |
| 8 | Save Document Metadata | Backend stores document information such as file name, type, size, workspace, and upload time. |
| 9 | Set Processing Status | System changes the document status to Processing. |
| 10 | Send Document to AI Service | Backend sends the document to the Python AI Service for processing. |
| 11 | Parse Document | AI Service parses the PDF/DOCX file. |
| 12 | Extract Text | AI Service extracts textual content from the document. |
| 13 | Extract Metadata | AI Service extracts page, section, and other relevant source metadata. |
| 14 | Chunk Document | Extracted text is divided into smaller chunks for retrieval. |
| 15 | Generate Embedding | AI Service converts document chunks into vector embeddings. |
| 16 | Store Chunks | Document chunks are stored in PostgreSQL. |
| 17 | Store Embeddings | Embeddings are stored in PostgreSQL using pgvector. |
| 18 | Complete Processing | System changes the document status to Completed. |
| 19 | Return Processing Result | Backend returns the processing result to the student. |
| 20 | Ready for Quiz Generation | The processed document becomes available for RAG-based quiz generation. |

&nbsp;

### 2.2 Outcome-Aligned Quiz Generation Process — Process Step Description

| \# | Process Step | Description |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| 1 | Select Course | Student selects the course for quiz generation. |
| 2 | Select Learning Outcomes | Student selects one or more predefined learning outcomes. |
| 3 | Configure Quiz | Student configures quiz parameters. |
| 4 | Set Question Count | Student specifies the number of questions to generate. |
| 5 | Set Difficulty | Student selects the desired difficulty level. |
| 6 | Request Quiz Generation | Student clicks the Generate Quiz button. |
| 7 | Authenticate Student | Backend verifies the student's authentication. |
| 8 | Check Workspace Permission | Backend verifies that the student can access the selected course/workspace. |
| 9 | Validate Quiz Configuration | System validates the question count, difficulty, learning outcomes, and other parameters. |
| 10 | Check Token Quota | System checks whether the student has sufficient token quota for generation. |
| 11 | Create Generation Request | Backend creates a quiz generation request. |
| 12 | Send Request to AI Service | Backend sends the request to the Python AI Service. |
| 13 | Create Retrieval Query | AI Service creates a retrieval query based on the course and learning outcomes. |
| 14 | Generate Query Embedding | The retrieval query is converted into an embedding vector. |
| 15 | Search Vector Database | The system searches pgvector for semantically similar document chunks. |
| 16 | Filter by Course / Workspace | Retrieved documents are restricted to the selected course/workspace. |
| 17 | Retrieve Relevant Chunks | The system selects the most relevant document chunks. |
| 18 | Build RAG Context | Retrieved chunks are combined into the context provided to the LLM. |
| 19 | Apply Prompt Constraints | System applies course, learning outcome, question format, and grounding constraints. |
| 20 | Generate Candidate Questions | LLM generates candidate questions and answer options. |
| 21 | Validate Question Structure | System validates the required question and option structure. |
| 22 | Validate Course Constraint | System checks whether the generated question is related to the selected course materials. |
| 23 | Validate Learning Outcome Alignment | System checks whether the question matches the selected learning outcome. |
| 24 | Validate Grounding | System verifies that the generated question can be supported by retrieved source content. |
| 25 | Map Question to Source | System maps the generated question to the relevant source chunk. |
| 26 | Create Citation | System creates citation information for the question. |
| 27 | Validate Evidence | System checks whether sufficient evidence exists to support the generated question. |
| 28 | Reject / Regenerate | Unsupported questions are rejected or regenerated. |
| 29 | Prepare Quiz | Valid questions are assembled into the final quiz. |
| 30 | Save Quiz | System saves the quiz and its metadata. |
| 31 | Save Questions | System saves the generated questions and options. |
| 32 | Save Citations | System stores citation information for the generated questions. |
| 33 | Update Token Usage | System updates the student's token usage/quota. |
| 34 | Return Quiz | Backend returns the generated quiz to the student. |
| 35 | Display Generated Quiz | Student views the generated quiz and source citations. |

# 3\. System Context and Architecture&nbsp;

### 3.1 C0 – Context Diagram&nbsp;

![][image5]

### 3.2 Context Description&nbsp;

The FPT RAG Lab is an AI-assisted web platform that enables students to generate Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-based, outcome-aligned multiple-choice quizzes strictly from their uploaded course documents. The system interacts with the following actors and external systems:

A. Actors (Users):

1. Student:  
   * Description: An FPT University student who uses the system to upload course materials, configure and generate outcome-aligned MCQ quizzes, take quizzes, and review results with source citations.  
   * Interactions: Uploads documents, generates and takes quizzes, reviews results and citations via HTTPS.  
2. Administrator:  
   * Description: A system administrator who manages users, courses, learning outcomes, token quotas, system policies, and monitors platform usage.  
   * Interactions: Manages users, courses, learning outcomes, token quotas, and system policies via HTTPS.

B. External Systems:

1. LLM API (Large Language Model API):  
   * Description: A Large Language Model API (e.g., OpenAI GPT / Google Gemini) used to generate quiz questions, answer options, explanations, and grounding validation from RAG context.  
   * Communication: The system sends RAG context \+ prompt constraints; it receives generated questions, options, explanations, and grounding validation (REST/JSON).  
2. Embedding API:  
   * Description: A text embedding service (e.g., OpenAI Embeddings / open-source model) that converts document chunks and retrieval queries into vector representations for semantic search.  
   * Communication: The system sends document chunks and retrieval queries; it receives vector embeddings for pgvector storage and semantic search (REST/JSON).  
3. Email Service:  
   * Description: A transactional email provider (e.g., SendGrid / SMTP) used to send account registration confirmations, password resets, and system notifications to users.  
   * Communication: The system sends account verification and notification emails (SMTP / REST).  
4. OCR Service:  
   * Description: An Optical Character Recognition service used to extract text from scanned or image-based PDF documents before chunking and embedding.  
   * Communication: The system sends scanned PDF pages; it receives extracted plain text for chunking (REST/JSON).

### 3.3 C1 – Container Diagram&nbsp;

![][image6]

### 3.4 Container Description&nbsp;

The FPT RAG Lab system is decomposed into the following containers (services):

A. Internal Containers:

1. Web Application:  
   * Description: The user interface for both Students and Administrators (role-based views). It handles login, course management, document upload, quiz configuration, taking quizzes, viewing results, and the admin dashboard.  
   * Interactions: Calls the Backend API.  
2. Backend API:  
   * Description: Handles core business logic: Authentication (JWT), Authorization (RBAC), orchestrating quiz generation, managing documents, quiz attempts, token tracking, and audit logging. It accesses relational data via EF Core / Npgsql.  
   * Interactions: Receives requests from the Web App; sends requests to the RAG/AI Service, Relational Database, File Storage, and Email Service.  
3. RAG / AI Service:  
   * Description: Handles specialized AI tasks: Document parsing, chunking, embedding generation (calls Embedding API), semantic retrieval (pgvector), RAG context building, prompt constraints, grounding validation, and citation mapping (calls LLM API).  
   * Interactions: Receives requests from the Backend API; interacts with the Vector Database, LLM API, and Embedding API.  
4. Relational Database:  
   * Technology: PostgreSQL (based on Npgsql).  
   * Description: Stores user information, courses, learning outcomes, document metadata, quizzes, questions, quiz attempts, token usage, and audit logs.  
   * Interactions: Reads/Writes business data from the Backend API.  
5. Vector Database:  
   * Technology: pgvector (integrated into PostgreSQL).  
   * Description: Stores document embeddings along with workspace metadata for semantic similarity queries. All queries must be filtered by workspace\_id.  
   * Interactions: Queried for vector similarity by the RAG/AI Service.  
6. File Storage:  
   * Description: Stores original PDF/DOCX files with random identifiers (UUIDs). Access control is managed through the backend.  
   * Interactions: Saves/Reads original document files from the Backend API.

B. External Systems (Connected via Backend/RAG Service):

* Email Service: Sends verification and notification emails.  
* LLM API: Generates questions, answers, explanations, and grounding validation.  
* Embedding API: Converts text into vector representations.  
* OCR Service: Extracts text from scanned/image-based PDFs.

# **III. User Requirements**

## **1\. Actors**

> * **Student:** Primary user who interacts with courses, uploads documents, generates outcome-aligned quizzes, takes quizzes, and views results with source citations.  
> * **Administrator:** Manages users, courses, learning outcomes, system policies, token quotas, and reviews system statistics.  
> * **AI/RAG Service:** External/Internal microservice handling document parsing, embedding generation, semantic search, LLM prompting, grounding validation, and citation mapping.

| **UC-25** | Chunk Document | System | Divide extracted document content into smaller chunks for retrieval and embedding generation. This use case is included in Process Document. |
| **UC-26** | Generate Embedding | System | Convert document chunks into vector representations for semantic retrieval. This use case is included in Process Document and interacts with the Vector Database. |
| **UC-27** | Store Vector | System | Store document embeddings and related metadata in PostgreSQL with pgvector. This use case is included in Process Document. |
| **UC-28** | Retrieve Relevant Context | System, Vector Database | Retrieve the most relevant personal document chunks based on the quiz generation request. This use case interacts with the Vector Database. |
| **UC-29** | Build RAG Context | System | Combine course information, learning outcomes, and retrieved personal document chunks into a context for the LLM. |
| **UC-30** | Apply Prompt Constraints | System | Apply constraints requiring generated questions to remain within the selected course, learning outcomes, and retrieved document content. This use case is included in Generate Questions. |
| **UC-31** | Generate Questions | System, LLM API | Generate quiz questions, options, and explanations using the RAG context and prompt constraints. This use case includes Apply Prompt Constraints. |
| **UC-32** | Validate Grounding | System, LLM API | Validate whether generated questions can be grounded in the retrieved personal document content and selected learning outcomes. |
| **UC-33** | Provide Citation | System | Attach source document references, page information, or relevant document chunks to generated questions. This use case is included in Generate Quiz. |
| **UC-34** | Refuse Generation | System | Refuse quiz generation when the requested content cannot be sufficiently grounded in the available personal study documents. This use case extends Validate Grounding. |
| **UC-35** | Save Quiz | System | Save successfully generated quizzes, questions, options, explanations, and citations for later use and review. |
| **UC-36** | Reuse Existing Quiz | System | Reuse a previously generated quiz when the same course, learning outcomes, configuration, and document context already exist, reducing unnecessary LLM token consumption. This use case is included in Generate Quiz. |
| **UC-37** | Submit Quiz | System | Receive and validate the student's quiz answers and finalize the quiz attempt. This use case includes Calculate Score. |
| **UC-38** | Calculate Score | System | Compare submitted answers with correct answers and calculate the student's quiz score. This use case is included in Submit Quiz. |
| **UC-39** | View Explanation | Student, System | Display explanations associated with quiz questions and answers.This use case is included in View Result. |
| **UC-40** | View Citation | Student, System | Display the source document and relevant content supporting a generated question. This use case is included in View Result and Review Previous Quiz. |
| **UC-41** | Check Token Quota | System | Check whether the student or role has sufficient token quota before performing an AI generation request. This use case is included in Generate Quiz. |
| **UC-42** | Track Token Usage | System | Record input tokens, output tokens, total tokens, model information, and estimated cost for AI requests. This use case is included in Generate Quiz. |

# **3\. Business Rules**

## **3.1 Authentication & User Management — BR-01 to BR-09**

| BR ID | Business Rule | Source | Type |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-01 | Users must provide all required information when registering. | UC-01 | Mandatory |
| BR-02 | The system must authenticate users using valid login credentials. | UC-02 | Mandatory |
| BR-03 | The system must support refresh tokens to maintain authenticated sessions. | UC-03 | Security |
| BR-04 | Users can view and update their personal information. | UC-04 | Functional |
| BR-05 | Users must be authenticated before accessing protected functions. | UC-21 | Security |
| BR-06 | The system must apply role-based access control for Student and Administrator roles. | UC-22 | Security |
| BR-07 | Backend authorization must be verified independently of frontend restrictions. | UC-22 | Security |
| BR-08 | Passwords must be stored as hashes and must never be stored in plaintext. | UC-01, UC-02 | Security |
| BR-09 | Authentication events must be logged for auditing purposes. | UC-21 | Audit |

---

## **3.2 Course Catalog — BR-10 to BR-15**

| BR ID | Business Rule | Source | Type |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-10 | Students can view the list of available courses. | UC-05 | Functional |
| BR-11 | Students can view course details and Learning Outcomes. | UC-06 | Functional |
| BR-12 | Administrators can create, update, activate, and deactivate courses. | UC-15 | Functional |
| BR-13 | Each course code must be unique. | UC-15 | Validation |
| BR-14 | Each course must have at least one Learning Outcome. | UC-15, UC-16 | Structural |
| BR-15 | Administrators can manage Learning Outcomes of courses. | UC-16 | Functional |

---

## **3.3 Document Management — BR-16 to BR-22**

| BR ID | Business Rule | Source | Type |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-16 | Students can upload PDF/DOCX documents only to their own personal workspace. | UC-07 | Mandatory |
| BR-17 | Personal documents must be isolated and used only for the respective student's learning and quiz generation. | UC-07 | Security |
| BR-18 | Uploaded files must be validated for file type, size, and system constraints. | UC-07 | Validation |
| BR-19 | Invalid files must be rejected with a clear error message. | UC-07 | Exception |
| BR-20 | Students can view only their own document list and document status. | UC-08 | Security |
| BR-21 | Documents must have one of the following statuses: Processing, Completed, or Failed. | UC-23 | Structural |
| BR-22 | A successful document upload must automatically trigger the RAG processing pipeline. | UC-07 | Process |

---

## **3.4 RAG Document Processing & Indexing — BR-23 to BR-32**

| BR ID | Business Rule | Source | Type |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-23 | The system must process uploaded personal documents. | UC-23 | Process |
| BR-24 | Document processing must include parsing, chunking, embedding generation, and vector storage. | UC-24–UC-27 | Process |
| BR-25 | The system must extract document content and metadata. | UC-24 | Functional |
| BR-26 | Document content must be divided into document chunks. | UC-25 | Technical |
| BR-27 | Each appropriate document chunk must be converted into a vector embedding. | UC-26 | Technical |
| BR-28 | Embeddings must be stored in PostgreSQL with pgvector. | UC-27 | Technical |
| BR-29 | Each chunk must retain source information such as document, page, section, and workspace. | UC-25–UC-27 | Traceability |
| BR-30 | RAG retrieval must retrieve chunks relevant to the quiz request. | UC-28 | Functional |
| BR-31 | Retrieval must be restricted to the current student's workspace. | UC-28 | Security |
| BR-32 | Every vector query must include a workspace filter. | UC-28 | Security |

---

## **3.5 Quiz Configuration & Generation — BR-33 to BR-45**

| BR ID | Business Rule | Source | Type |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-33 | Students can configure Learning Outcomes, question count, difficulty, and quiz settings. | UC-09 | Functional |
| BR-34 | A quiz must be generated based on the selected Course, Learning Outcomes, quiz configuration, and personal documents. | UC-10 | Mandatory |
| BR-35 | The RAG context must combine Course information, Learning Outcomes, and retrieved document chunks. | UC-10 | Process |
| BR-36 | Generated questions must be constrained to the selected Course, Learning Outcomes, and retrieved documents. | UC-10 | Safety |
| BR-37 | The LLM must generate questions, answer options, and explanations. | UC-31 | Functional |
| BR-38 | Generated questions must be validated against the source documents and Learning Outcomes. | UC-33 | Validation |
| BR-39 | Generated questions must contain appropriate citations or source references. | UC-33 | Traceability |
| BR-40 | The system must refuse quiz generation when there is insufficient information for grounding. | UC-34 | Safety |
| BR-41 | Quizzes, questions, options, explanations, and citations must be stored. | UC-35 | Persistence |
| BR-42 | The system must reuse an equivalent existing quiz to reduce token consumption. | UC-36 | Optimization |
| BR-43 | Each generated question must have a citation when sufficient supporting evidence is available. | UC-33 | Traceability |
| BR-44 | Questions that fail grounding, structure, or Learning Outcome alignment must be rejected or regenerated. | UC-34 | Validation |
| BR-45 | Quiz generation must combine retrieval, context building, prompt constraints, LLM generation, grounding, and citation mapping. | UC-28–UC-35 | Process |

| BR ID | Business Rule | Source | Type |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-46 | Students can take generated quizzes. | UC-11 | Functional |
| BR-47 | The system must validate and finalize answers when a student submits a quiz. | UC-12 | Validation |
| BR-48 | The system must compare submitted answers with correct answers to calculate the score. | UC-12 | Functional |
| BR-49 | Students can view their score, correct answers, explanations, and citations. | UC-13 | Functional |
| BR-50 | Question explanations must be displayed after quiz completion. | UC-13 | Functional |
| BR-51 | Relevant source or supporting content must be displayed for each question. | UC-13 | Traceability |
| BR-52 | The system must store quiz attempts, answers, scores, and submission timestamps. | UC-12 | Audit |
| BR-53 | The system must warn or request confirmation when a student submits a quiz with unanswered questions. | UC-12 | Validation |

| BR ID | Business Rule | Source | Type |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-54 | Students can view their previous quizzes and attempts. | UC-14 | Functional |
| BR-55 | Students can review completed quizzes including questions, answers, explanations, and citations. | UC-14 | Functional |
| BR-56 | Reviewing a previous quiz must not consume LLM tokens. | UC-14 | Optimization |
| BR-57 | Students can retry a previous quiz without generating a new quiz through the LLM. | UC-14 | Optimization |

| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |

| BR-64 | Administrators can view system statistics. | UC-19 | Functional |
| BR-65 | Administrators can configure system policies. | UC-20 | Functional |

| BR ID | Business Rule | Source | Type |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |

| BR-70 | Administrator manages users, courses, Learning Outcomes, policies, quotas, and statistics. | UC-15–UC-20 | Role |
| BR-71 | The AI/RAG Service handles parsing, embeddings, retrieval, LLM interaction, prompting, grounding, and citation mapping. | UC-23–UC-35 | Architectural |

## **3.11 Data Isolation & Security — BR-74 to BR-79**

| BR ID | Business Rule | Source | Type |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-74 | Personal documents must be isolated by Student/Workspace. | UC-28 | Security |
| BR-75 | The system must prevent students from accessing documents belonging to other students. | UC-28 | Security |
| BR-76 | User data must be controlled through the Backend layer; the AI Service must not directly access user data without authorization. | UC-21, UC-28 | Security |
| BR-77 | The Backend must verify workspace permissions before accessing workspace data. | UC-28 | Security |
| BR-78 | LLM API keys must not be exposed to the frontend and must be stored securely in the backend environment. | UC-31 | Security |

## **3.12 Technical Constraints & Architecture — BR-80 to BR-85**

| BR ID | Business Rule | Source | Type |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-80 | The system must contain the major components defined in the system architecture. | C1 Container | Architectural |
| BR-81 | The Backend is responsible for authentication, course, document, quiz, and AI/RAG orchestration. | C1 Container | Architectural |
| BR-82 | The Python AI/RAG Service is responsible for document processing and the RAG pipeline. | C1 Container | Architectural |
| BR-83 | PostgreSQL with pgvector must be used for relational and vector data. | C1 Container | Technical |
| BR-84 | The system supports PDF and DOCX documents. | UC-07 | Constraint |
| BR-85 | Internet connectivity is required to use cloud-based AI APIs. | C1 Container | Constraint |

## **3.13 Scope Limitations — BR-86 to BR-93**

| BR ID | Business Rule | Source | Type |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-86 | Quiz quality depends on the quality and content of the uploaded documents. | UC-10 | Constraint |
| BR-87 | Scanned documents may require OCR to process their content. | UC-24 | Constraint |
| BR-88 | LLM-generated content must still be validated through grounding and validation mechanisms. | UC-33, UC-34 | Safety |
| BR-89 | Large documents may require more processing time. | UC-23–UC-27 | Constraint |
| BR-90 | The AI API may experience errors, timeouts, or unavailability. | UC-31 | Exception |
| BR-91 | Retrieval quality depends on the chunking and embedding strategy. | UC-25–UC-30 | Technical |
| BR-92 | The system supports only file formats and file sizes within the configured limits. | UC-07 | Constraint |
| BR-93 | Functions outside the defined system scope are not considered system requirements. | Scope | Constraint |

| BR ID | Business Rule | Source | Type |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| BR-94 | Document upload must follow the process of validation → storage → parsing → chunking → embedding → vector storage. | UC-07, UC-23–UC-27 | Process |
| BR-95 | Quiz generation must follow the process of configuration → quota check → retrieval → context building → generation → grounding → citation → saving. | UC-09, UC-10, UC-28–UC-35 | Process |
| BR-96 | Quiz execution must follow the process of taking the quiz → submission → scoring → result → review. | UC-11–UC-14, UC-37–UC-40 | Process |
| BR-97 | Administration must follow the process of authentication → authorization → management → monitoring → statistics/audit. | UC-15–UC-20 | Process |
